questions.subject: COMPARATIVE_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Define democracy as rule by the people
questions.stem: In the amateur astronomer's log, a regime is democratic only when citizens freely choose their leaders by election.

options.text: A regime is democratic when citizens freely choose leaders by election
A regime is democratic when one party rules to keep order
A regime is democratic when courts enforce strict laws
options.misconception: confuses rule of law with democracy

options.text: A regime is democratic when the military guards borders

questions.explanation: Democracy rests on popular sovereignty through free elections; order, courts, or security alone do not establish democratic rule.
questions.hint: Look for citizen choice of leaders.

questions.subject: COMPARATIVE_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Identify authoritarian rule by concentrated power
questions.stem: The log notes a state where one leader holds power without real checks; explain why this is authoritarian.

answer.exemplar: Authoritarian rule concentrates power in one leader or small group with weak checks, so citizens cannot freely replace leaders or contest decisions.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian systems limit political competition and checks; the absence of free replacement of leaders marks them as non-democratic.
questions.hint: Focus on concentrated power and weak checks.
